items.t: Retreat bookings route through our partners, not a direct checkout — and why
items.x: medium priority We made a values decision about how retreat bookings work on I Am One Self, and wanted to share the reasoning, not just the outcome. What changed Bookings for our partner retreat centers — Sachamama, Inca Shipiba, and Garden of Peace — route exclusively through Retreat Guru, Aya Advisors, and The Third Wave. We considered building a direct booking/checkout flow on our own site and chose not to. We also removed pricing comparisons between our own partner centers from the site. You'll still find pricing where we compare against centers outside our partner network — that's honest differentiation. But ranking our own partners against each other by price didn't sit right with what we're building.

items.s: Search silently didn't work at all before this fix — now it does, on every page.
items.x: high priority TL;DR: Search silently didn't work at all before this fix — now it does, on every page. Read the full story → The site's search box looked normal but never returned results. The real cause, and the deeper technical write up, lives in the library — the Pagefind ES module fix. What changed Search now works across the whole site. Why it mattered A search box that silently does nothing is worse than no search box at all — it looks like it should work, so a visitor assumes their query just didn't match anything, when actually nothing was searched at all.

items.s: A donate modal rendered pinned to a 64px header instead of the full viewport -- a real CSS gotcha worth knowing.
items.x: TL;DR: Any ancestor with backdrop filter (or filter / transform ) becomes the containing block for its position: fixed descendants a donate modal was rendering pinned to a 64px header instead of the full viewport until this was found. Read the full story → The bug A donation modal on David Amaringo's site was supposed to overlay the entire viewport when opened. Instead, it rendered as a tiny strip pinned to the site's 64px tall header — as if the modal believed the header, not the browser window, was the full extent of the page. items.s: Search silently failed because pagefind.js is an ES module with no window.pagefind global -- fixed with a dynamic import().
items.x: TL;DR: pagefind.js is an ES module, not a classic script a plain <script> tag injection never creates the expected window.pagefind global, so search silently did nothing. Fixed with a dynamic import() instead. Read the full story → The bug Site search looked implemented — a search box existed, submitting a query didn't error — but no results ever came back, for any query, ever. The real cause The search feature uses Pagefind, a static site search library that builds its index at deploy time. Pagefind's output, pagefind.js , is an ES module — it uses export statements internally and expects to be loaded via import , not injected as a classic tag. The code was doing the latter: dynamical
